comments.author: @leechumbley5440
comments.text: I had the privilege to visit Göbekli Tepe twice. The first time was in 2014 when every thing was open air, an archaeological dig in progress and only known to specialists. We were shown around by Klaus Schmidt personally. I visited again several years later, when a protective roof and walkway had been built. I read Klaus Schmidt’s book. Thank you for this marvelous and scholarly update of ongoing research and new finds. In particular I was glad to learn of the discovery of seasonal dwellings, human figures and cereal preparation, as well as excavations on scattered sites in the area with T-shaped megaliths. That genetically ancient einkorn grew in the hills was known, as was evidence suggesting beer brewing, when we first visited in 2014. One truly gets a feeling of awe. Is this indeed the 1st temple of mankind? One of the first sites of wheat as a foodstuff? The makers were hunters and gatherers, not yet the first farmers in this aceramic time. You have prepared this video with great care and erudition. Thank you.

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: What a privilege, to see it as an open-air dig and then again under the roof, and to be shown around by Klaus Schmidt himself. Having seen both versions of the site, which one stayed with you more: the raw excavation or the protected walkway?
